methodological_questions: How to define and measure lineup coverage reliably from play-type possession records?
How to test within-team variation of coverage?
How to separate coverage effect from overall talent and simple role counts?
How to control for player talent when testing coverage?
What are potential confounders (e.g., opponent strength, game context) and how to address them?
evidence_establishes: No prior project studies were retrieved for this specific question, so nothing is established.
evidence_does_not_establish: The feasibility of reliably defining organizer/shaper/terminal roles from the available data.
The magnitude of lineup-coverage variation within teams.
The separability of coverage effects from overall talent and role counts.
The behavior of talent controls in this context.
own_inferences: The question can be sharpened into a testable form: define roles via clustering of play-type distributions from past seasons; define coverage as a binary indicator per lineup (or per stint) of having at least one player in each role; estimate the effect of coverage on offensive/defensive efficiency within team, controlling for player fixed effects or rolling player quality metrics.
Within-team variation in coverage is plausible because injuries, substitutions, and tactical adjustments change role availability.
Separability from talent can be tested by including player-level quality ratings or past performance metrics in the model.
Potential endogeneity must be addressed: lineups are not randomly assigned, and coverage may correlate with game situation.
uncertainties: Whether the organizer/shaper/terminal taxonomy maps cleanly onto NBA play-type data; the roles may overlap or be ambiguous for many players.
Whether sufficient within-team variation exists across the 90 team-seasons and 420,993 possessions.
Whether the talent control fully addresses confounding from coaching decisions and matchup effects.
Whether the outcome (e.g., points per possession) is measured at the appropriate level (possession, stint, or game).
Potential look-ahead bias if role definitions use data from the same games tested.

historical_effect.explanation: No prior studies were retrieved, so the decision was based solely on the current task's data and methodological assessment.

blocking_constraints.text: The role definitions (organizer, shaper, terminal) must be reliable and stable across seasons; otherwise coverage measurement is noisy and may produce spurious results.
If most lineups already contain at least one of each role, the exposure variation may be too small to estimate effects with adequate power.

prior_work.summary: No prior studies by this project on lineup coverage with organizer/shaper/terminal roles were returned.

risks.text: The classification of players into organizer, shaper, terminal roles from play-type data may be unreliable if the taxonomy is not well-defined or if many players exhibit hybrid profiles.
If the condition '>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal' is nearly always satisfied in NBA lineups, coverage will lack variation, making an effect test underpowered.
If coverage is very common, the base rate may be too high to identify a meaningful effect, or the comparison group may be too small.
Coaching decisions, opponent matchups, game situation, and correlated player quality can confound the coverage-performance relationship.
If roles are derived from the same game data used to test coverage effects, look-ahead bias may inflate the apparent effect.
Lineup changes are often reactive to performance; if a lineup underperforms, a substitution may alter coverage, creating reverse causality.
Testing multiple outcomes (e.g., offensive rating, defensive rating, net rating) and sub-group analyses could inflate false-positive risk.
Although the overall possession count is large, the effective sample at the unique-lineup or stint level may be limited, particularly for rare coverage states.

design.estimand: The within-team effect of lineup coverage (binary: >=1 player classified as organizer, >=1 as shaper, >=1 as terminal) on points scored per 100 possessions (offensive rating) and points allowed per 100 possessions (defensive rating), holding constant player quality.
design.unit: Stint (a continuous segment of a game where neither team changes personnel), or possession-level, depending on role assignment stability.
design.sample: All regular-season games from 2022-23 through 2025-26, excluding garbage time (defined as game in last 5 minutes with point differential >20, or coach's challenge situations).
design.power: Simulation-based power analysis using pilot data from the earliest season (2022-23) to detect a 1.5-point per 100 possessions effect, assuming an intra-team coverage variation prevalence of at least 15% of stints.
design.controls: Player fixed effects (or random effects if crossed), team-season fixed effects, opponent strength (opponent defensive/offensive rating from prior games), rest days, home/away, and a rolling player quality metric (e.g., RAPM or simple plus-minus over the previous 20 games) as a continuous talent control.
design.falsification: Test whether coverage affects outcomes that should be unaffected (e.g., free-throw percentage of the opponent, or next-game performance of the same players). Also, test for reverse causality by examining whether prior stint performance predicts subsequent coverage changes.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify primary outcomes (offensive rating and net rating), use Benjamini-Hochberg correction for any exploratory sub-analyses, and report all specifications in a pre-analysis plan.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null hypothesis of no coverage effect if the coverage coefficient's 95% confidence interval excludes zero and the effect is stable across multiple role-definition sensitivity analyses (e.g., stricter/looser role assignment thresholds).
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular-season data as available on 2026-07-13; roles defined using a hold-out season (2022-23) to avoid look-ahead.

How to test within-team variation of coverage?
How to separate coverage effect from overall talent and role counts?
How to control for player talent when testing coverage?
Potential confounders for lineup coverage effects on performance?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

{"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["lineup coverage", "organizer", "shaper", "terminal", "within-team variation", "talent control", "role coverage", "structural roles"], "methodological_questions": ["How to define and measure lineup coverage reliably?", "How to test within-team variation of coverage?", "How to separate coverage effect from overall talent and role counts?", "How to control for player talent when testing coverage?", "Potential confounders for lineup coverage effects on performance?"], "query": "lineup coverage organizer shaper terminal within-team variation talent control separable from counts"}}

reasoning_details.text:
We need to identify research concepts and methodological questions from the research question: "Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves."

The research question is about structural roles: organizer, shaper, terminal. These are presumably defined in the project's glossary. "Lineup coverage" means whether a lineup has at least one player of each role. So the question is: does lineup coverage (i.e., having at least one organizer, one shaper, and one terminal) vary within a team (i.e., for a given team, different lineups have different coverage status), is it separable from talent and counts (i.e., not just a function of overall team talent or number of players in each role), and does talent control behave (i.e., when controlling for talent, the effect of coverage remains?). So we need to retrieve relevant history.

Research concepts: "lineup coverage", "organizer", "shaper", "terminal", "within-team variation", "talent control", "separable from talent/counts". Methodological questions: how to measure lineup coverage (role definitions), how to handle within-team variation (team fixed effects? multilevel?), how to control for talent (player-level metrics like EPM, RAPM?), confounding, sample size/power for rare coverage combinations, etc.

We'll query retrieve_history with appropriate concepts and questions. Use terms exactly as they might appear in the project. Let's construct a query string: "lineup coverage organizer shaper terminal within-team variation talent control separable". We'll list research_concepts and methodological_questions accordingly.

We must return only the retrieval call.

We are in stage 2. The retrieval returned no results. So we have no historical evidence from this project's earlier studies. We need to complete the assessment.

We need to decide whether the research question can be answered. The question: "Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves."

Let's parse: "lineup coverage" defined as having at least one player of each role type: organizer, shaper, terminal. So a lineup is "covered" if it has >=1 organizer, >=1 shaper, >=1 terminal. These roles are presumably defined from some taxonomy. The research question appears to be about whether this coverage varies within a team over lineups/possessions, whether its effect is separable from overall talent level and simple counts of players (e.g., number of stars), and whether controlling for talent works.

The data: NBA per-game data from 2022-23 through 2025-26 (multiple seasons), play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, defensive matchups, box-score, and derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database. Units: 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons.

We need to assess testability. Let's consider the concepts.

Research concepts: lineup coverage, organizer, shaper, terminal, within-team variation, talent control.

Methodological questions: how to define roles reliably, how to measure coverage, how to test within-team variation, separating coverage from talent, controlling for player talent, potential confounders.

Now, we must produce the output. Since no historical evidence was returned, we set historical_evidence and failed_approaches to empty lists. evidence_establishes and evidence_does_not_establish should reflect that no prior evidence was found. own_inferences: we need to infer from the task description whether the question is testable.

We need to identify risks. Let's think: the roles "organizer, shaper, terminal" are presumably derived from play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points). This implies we need to assign each player to one of these roles. That classification might be based on their play types. This raises issues: MEASURE_RELIABILITY (role assignment reliability), EXPOSURE_SPARSITY (some lineups may rarely have all three roles), OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL (the coverage label might be derived from the same play-by-play data used to measure outcomes, causing circularity if not careful), LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD if roles are defined from the same games, etc. Also, "coverage >=1 organizer, shaper, terminal" might be rare if most lineups already have that, so BASE_RATE issue. There could be CONFOUNDING: talented teams may have players who cover multiple roles, so coverage might be collinear with talent. MECHANICAL_FLOOR: if the outcome metric is points per possession, etc., coverage might mechanically relate to having enough playmakers. SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER: with 90 team-seasons and many possessions, but the analysis might be at lineup level, which could have fewer unique lineups. However, there are many possessions.

The question states "Lineup coverage ... varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves." This seems like they want to test: (1) whether lineup coverage varies within teams (i.e., different lineups have different coverage status), (2) whether the effect of coverage on performance is separable from sheer talent level and from just the counts of players (like total points scored average), and (3) whether controlling for talent (e.g., player fixed effects) behaves as expected (maybe removing bias). So it's a series of tests. The question is fairly vague: "behaves" is ambiguous. Perhaps they want to pre-register a design to test the hypothesis that lineup coverage (having all three roles) improves performance beyond what would be expected from the sum of individual talents.

Testability: I think it is testable if roles can be defined meaningfully from play-type data. The graph database has initiator and play type per possession. So we could classify players by their tendency to initiate certain play types (e.g., organizer might be someone who frequently initiates plays that lead to assists; shaper might be a player who creates off-ball movement; terminal might be a finisher). But these labels must be defined ex-ante and reliably. There's risk of post-hoc rationalization. However, the data might allow clustering of players based on play-type distributions.

Potential confounders: opponent strength, game context, fatigue, etc.

We need to make a decision. I'd say proceed_with_changes because the question as posed is a bit vague and needs sharper definitions of roles, outcome, and talent control. The design should specify how roles are defined, how coverage is measured (at possession level? lineup level?), how within-team variation is tested, and how talent control is implemented (e.g., using player fixed effects or prior performance metrics). Also, need to ensure no lookahead bias: roles should be defined from past data or a separate set. With multiple seasons, we can use one season to define and another to test.

Given no historical evidence, the decision cannot be changed by it. So historical_effect: no_historical_evidence.

evidence_does_not_establish: ["The feasibility of reliably defining organizer/shaper/terminal roles from the available data, the magnitude of lineup coverage variation, the separability of coverage effects from talent, and the behavior of talent controls."]

own_inferences: ["The question can be sharpened into a testable form: define roles via clustering play-type distributions from past seasons; define coverage as a binary indicator per lineup (or per stretch) of having at least one player in each role; estimate the effect of coverage on offensive/defensive efficiency within team, controlling for player fixed effects or rolling player quality metrics; test whether coverage varies within teams over time."]

uncertainties: ["Whether the organiser/shaper/terminal taxonomy maps cleanly onto NBA play-type data; whether sufficient within-team variation exists; whether the talent control fully addresses endogeneity of lineups; whether the outcome is measured at the appropriate level (possession or stint)."]

testability: I'd give p_testable = 0.7, blocking_constraints: maybe EXPOSURE_SPARSITY if many teams always have all three roles; but I'll list that as a risk. For blocking constraints, we need codes that could block testability. I'd say MEASURE_RELIABILITY if role definitions are unreliable. Also BASE_RATE if coverage is almost always 1. But these are risks that could be mitigated. I'll set p_testable to 0.7.

risks: list the relevant risk codes.

predicted_outcome: I'm not sure; I'd guess if the role taxonomy is well-designed, there might be an effect, but it could be artifact. I'll assign probabilities: supported 0.4, rejected 0.2, untestable 0.1, artifact 0.15, uncertain 0.15. Sum to 1.

decision: proceed_with_changes, because need to operationalize roles and design pre-registration.
